<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 50 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f485a6e345ca070986119353bd098132324ac1d` — the merge of head `082f766bf69f702411796717955551f9db58aeb3` into base `bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f485a6e345ca070986119353bd098132324ac1d && git checkout 5f485a6e345ca070986119353bd098132324ac1d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589 082f766bf69f702411796717955551f9db58aeb3 && git checkout -B drift-repro bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589 && git merge --no-ff 082f766bf69f702411796717955551f9db58aeb3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bacb3e6a0ff6e8bfdeade49d6830e34fb5522589` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`AutomationResult.code` gains `'RESUME_CHILD_PENDING'`** (`contracts/automation-service.ts`, union + bullet) — right. Triage 6515324504 ruled B and named this spelling (name is the maintainer's at approval). The bullet states the 409 mapping, that nothing moves, that `error` names the child run id, and that it is deliberately distinct from `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` (benign vs. "resume a different id") — matches the ruling's reason for B.
2. **`TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.code` enum gains the same member** (`automation-api.zod.ts`) — right; the file's own docblock requires the mirror, and `automation-api.zod.test.ts` binds `TriggerFlowResponse['data']` to `AutomationResult` at compile time, so the pair cannot drift.
3. **`ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/service-automation']` gains one row**, alphabetically before `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` — right. The emitter is `run-resume.ts` (this package), so the row is identity, not provenance; the row comment follows its neighbours' `[#NNNN]` convention (ledger comments are not runtime strings).
4. **`RESUME_REFUSAL_ROWS` gains `['RESUME_CHILD_PENDING', 409]`** (`runtime/domains/automation.ts`) — right. ONE table serves both the REST resume arm and the MCP `resume_run` tool via `classifyResumeResult`, so both doors answer 409 with `details.code` promoted verbatim; the arm's status comment and the "seven coded rows" count are updated; `automation-resume-refusal-codes.test.ts` floor pins the seventh key and its parse as an `ErrorCode`; `mcp-resume-run.test.ts` adds the row. Correctly NOT added: `RESTORE_REFUSAL_STATUS` (the restore door; its `SuspensionRestoreRefusal` union is unchanged) and `RETRYABLE_RESUME_REFUSAL_CODES` (see ④).
5. **`AutomationEngine.resume(runId)` accept set narrowed**: a resume addressed to a run whose linked-run chain holds a `map:` link with a still-suspended item child answers `{ success:false, code:'RESUME_CHILD_PENDING', error: "...Resume run 'ITEM' instead..." }` before any state is touched — right, this is the triage ruling verbatim (refused, coded 409, names the child, nothing advances, orphaned suspension no longer created).
6. **Private rename `resolveEffectiveSuspension` → `resolveSuspensionChain`** (returns the loaded chain, caller first) — no public surface: `RunResumeHost` and `MAP_ITEM_PENDING_REFUSAL_CODE` are module exports of `run-resume.ts` that `src/index.ts` does not re-export, so nothing on the package entry or `check:api-surface` moves.
7. **`LINKED_RUN_PREFIXES` docblock** now states the refusal instead of describing the advance as accepted — right; triage asked for exactly this update.
8. **`content/docs/references/api/*.mdx`** — generated output (+353 enum members), not reviewed; consistent with the enum/ledger change.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/27877-map-parent-resume-refusal.md`: `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime` all **`patch`**; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; BREAKING banner; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why.

- **Level — right.** AGENTS.md step 3 / ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone; a new member of a RESPONSE code enum is nothing a metadata author writes, so `none` is the true kind and `none` takes `patch` on every introduced entry. The spec "widening" of the wire vocabulary does not lift the level under ruling A, and `check:changeset-no-major`'s Check Changeset job is green on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes` — right**, per triage 6515324504 (「协议新增定 p1」; the seat's earlier `no (narrowing)` does not fit a new enum value).
- **Arm `(narrowing)` — right.** Both directions occur (a previously accepted call is now refused; a response enum gains a member), the closed pair allows at most one arm, and the one that carries the BREAKING signal the ADR-0087 gate and the queue guard read is `(narrowing)`. `none` beside `(narrowing)` is the "non-protocol narrowing ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner" lane the gate names explicitly.
- **ADR-0087 disposition — right.** No authorable key added, removed, renamed or re-shaped; a refusal before any state is touched leaves no stored shape to migrate; `no-migration-prescription` is a member of `CATEGORIES`; `check:adr-0087-registration` (Lint · CI, release & engine gates) is green on this head.
- **Migration prose — present**: Before / Now / Unchanged / New code / Who sees it / The remedy (resume the named item run).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6515519800 (written at 7edf37b4) and the PR body (same vintage) — every flag answered or escalated:

1. **`open_questions[0]` (which code)** — ANSWERED by triage 6515324504: B. The tree implements B in full (union, enum, ledger, runtime row, constant `MAP_ITEM_PENDING_REFUSAL_CODE = 'RESUME_CHILD_PENDING'`, changeset `Now.` line). Closed.
2. **Deviation "placeholder `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`"** — superseded by B; no placeholder remains in the tree (`git grep RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` finds every stamp, pin, row and doc; no `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` is constructed for this refusal).
3. **Deviation "scratch test `src/tmp-measure-27877.test.ts` deleted before commit"** — confirmed absent from the file list and the tree.
4. **Deviation "line_budget +327/-35 across 6 files"** — the head is +361/-40 across 15 files after B (spec ×3, runtime ×3, docs ×3, changeset); within reason for a protocol addition the ruling ordered.
5. **`out_of_scope_findings[0]`: a `map:` link whose item run is GONE (cancelled via `cancelRun`, which does not touch the parent) still lets a parent-id resume advance past that item** — "noted, not filed". ESCALATED to the lane seat as a card to file: it is reproducible and measured (the two forgery pins in `resume-authority-gate.test.ts` now construct exactly that state), and PD #10 files a reproducible defect rather than noting it. Not this PR's: triage's ruling covers the still-suspended item only, and refusing the gone-item shape would need its own ruling (the map re-entry pushes `$mapItemOutput ?? null` for it). Non-blocking.
6. **Acceptance note: the child run id is carried only in `error` text; `AutomationResult` has no structured member** — ACCEPTED as declared. The ruling says the 409 "names the child run id", and the message does; `classifyResumeResult` serves `details.code` only. A structured `details.childRunId` would be a spec addition under its own card (the dev did not sneak it in — right).
7. **Dogfood battery** — reported green on 7edf37b4 (357 files / 2875 tests), not on this head; the head differs by the spec/runtime/docs commits and the constant's spelling. The head's Dogfood Regression Gate check is success. Whether the lane owes a battery re-run on the final head is the seat's call per the claim's own `Container & model` line; not a contract finding.
8. **PR body stale lines (written before triage's answer; the relay cannot re-edit) — the seat's ACCEPT must carry these corrections**, judged against the tree:
   - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` → `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the changeset already says `yes`; ruling A grades on `Metadata-protocol: none`, so `yes` + `patch` passes Check Changeset — see ②).
   - 维护者速读 · 风险与回滚: 「拒绝码暂用 `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS` 占位,是否换新码等分诊答复」→ the code is `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING`, ruled B in 6515324504; 「需要你做的」: the maintainer's one act is to confirm the code's NAME at approval.
   - Measured table, After column: `code RESUME_IN_PROGRESS (see Open question)` → `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING`.
   - "## Open question" section → resolved (B); the surface widened to `packages/spec` (union, enum, ledger) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` (one 409 row), granted in 6515324504.
   - "What changes · Changeset": `@objectstack/service-automation patch` → three packages `patch` (`spec`, `runtime`, `service-automation`), `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.
   - "Verification" is on 7edf37b4; the head is 082f766b (spec/runtime/docs + the constant spelled as an annotated `const` so `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`'s `declaredInitializers` resolves it — the `satisfies` form is not a reducible initializer).
   - "Measured" table and "Tests" sections are otherwise accurate against the tree.

### ④ Design judgment

Face files, each held against the code it cites and the scenarios the card is accepted against:

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`** — the new bullet's claims each hold in the tree: 409 (runtime row 4 above); "directly, or through the run a `subflow` node waits on" (the chain walk follows `subflow:` then `map:`; test 4 pins it); "`error` names the child run id" (`refuseMapItemSkip` message); "the map continues when that child completes" (up-bubble via `resumeInternal`; test 3). Union order places it beside `RESUME_IN_PROGRESS`. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`** — mirror of the union; compile-time pin exists. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`** — row under the emitting package, alphabetical, 409 noted. `check:error-code-provenance` / `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`: the stamp site is `code: MAP_ITEM_PENDING_REFUSAL_CODE` (the `objlitconst` shape), resolved through `resolveConstant` → `declaredInitializers`, whose regex is `const NAME(: Type)? = ...;` — the head's annotated-const spelling is exactly that form, and the Lint · repo & tooling gates job is green. Holds.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`** — one row, one shared table, two doors agree; fallback text carries no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring`). MCP reachability note: a map parent's suspension row carries no `screen` (the map suspend arm sets none), so `resumeActionRun` step 5 refuses 409 before `resume` is called; the shared row still makes the doors agree if a surfaced screen ever reaches it. Holds.

**`packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`** — `resolveSuspensionChain` returns the loaded chain; a gone child row ends the chain at the `map:` link (so scenario 4 is NOT refused — a finished/failed/cancelled item leaves nothing behind the link and `refuseMapItemSkip` requires a successor); the depth-bound exit pushes the last loaded run. Docblocks on `resume`, `refuseGatedResume`, `LINKED_RUN_PREFIXES` state the ruling. Holds — with one should-fix below.

**`packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts`** — the gate's new order: resolve chain → judge AUTHORITY on the deepest run first (a service-owned item still answers 403 at every id, so a caller is never sent to a door that also refuses; the service stamp is still the recorded decision's tail) → otherwise `refuseMapItemSkip`, which refuses on the DEEPEST `map:` link with a successor, whatever the signal carries. Break attempts, each against the tree:

1. **Parent-id resume of a map whose item is still suspended** → chain `[parent(map:item), item]`, item authority `any` → `refuseMapItemSkip` i=0 → `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` naming `item.runId`; returned from `refuseGatedResume` before `resumeInternal`, so no `forgetSuspendedRun`, `$mapState` stays `{started:1, results:[]}`, item stays in `listSuspendedRuns()`, no `completed` row. Test 1 pins every one of those; test 2 pins the service-stamped variant. Holds.
2. **Resuming the child id** → chain `[item]`, no `map:` link → gate null → `resumeInternal(item)` → up-bubble `resumeInternal(parent)` re-runs the map (not gated) → parks on item 2 → second child resume completes the parent. Test 3. Holds.
3. **`subflow:` parent-id resume** → chain `[parent(subflow:child), child]`, no `map:` link → delegated as before. Test 5. A `subflow` over a parked `map` → chain `[outer, batch(map:item), item]` → refused at the outer id naming `item`, message says "waiting on run 'batch'". Test 4. Holds.
4. **Map whose item already finished/failed/cancelled** → child row gone → chain `[parent]` → no successor → null → `resumeInternal`. The two forgery pins in `resume-authority-gate.test.ts` cancel the item first and still reach `INVALID_SIGNAL`. Holds (and is the shape of ③.5).
5. **Consistency and consumers** — union, enum, ledger, runtime row (409), MCP (shared table) agree. Deliberately NOT in `RETRYABLE_RESUME_REFUSAL_CODES`: that set is what `resumeInternal` answers to a `subflow` parent delegating down (`run-resume.ts` ~L1218) and the delegation calls `resumeInternal`, which never runs the gate, so the code can never arrive there — adding it would be dead. Approvals: `serviceResume` resumes the approval's OWN run id (a leaf; its correlation is never `map:`), so the refusal is unreachable from approvals; if it ever arrived, `resumeCodeOf(err) === 'RESUME_IN_PROGRESS'` is the only tolerated arm and everything else falls through to the loud `[approvals] resume failed` log with `repairable: false` — safe fall-through, not a silent skip. Wait-node timer wake / boot re-arm resume the wait run's own id (a leaf; the `waitUntil` variable is keyed on the parked node, so a map parent never qualifies) — unreachable; its `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`-only keep-armed arm is unaffected. `ResumeFailureReport.code` (approvals contract) is `ErrorCode`, which the ledger row makes the new code a member of. Holds.
6. **Runtime strings** carry no tracker number (the `#27877` references are in comments and the ledger row comment only). Holds.

Findings:

- **should-fix (non-blocking)** — `engine.ts` `resolveSuspensionChain`: `seen` is seeded with child ids only, never the root `runId`, so a corrupt correlation cycle A→B→A yields the chain `[A, B, A]` and `refuseMapItemSkip` refuses naming the caller's own run id as "the run to resume instead".
